verses.1: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes in the dispersion, greetings.
verses.2: Consider it all joy, brothers, when you fall into various trials,
verses.3: understanding that the testing of your faith produces endurance;
verses.4: but endurance must have a work to complete, so that you may be perfect and complete, lacking nothing.
verses.5: If any one of you lacks wisdom, let him ask from the giving God, who gives to all without charge and does not rebuke, and it will be given to him;
verses.6: let him ask in faith, not doubting at all, for the one who doubts is like a wave of the sea being tossed and driven by the wind;
verses.7: for let not that man suppose he will receive anything from the Lord,
verses.8: a man double-minded, unstable in all his ways.
verses.9: But let the brother who is lowly boast in his exaltation,
verses.10: and the rich in his humiliation, because like a flower of grass he will pass away.
verses.11: For the sun arose with the scorching heat and withered the grass, and the flower of it fell, and the beauty of its face perished; so will the rich perish in his ways.
verses.12: Happy is the man who endures testing, for when he has been tested, he will receive the crown of life, which the Lord has promised to those who love Him.
verses.13: Let no one being tested say, "From God I am tested," for God is not tested by evil, nor does He test anyone.
verses.14: But each one is tested by being drawn away and enticed by his own desire;
verses.15: then the desire having seized gives birth to sin, and the sin having become complete brings forth death.
verses.16: Do not be led astray, brothers beloved.
verses.17: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom there is no variation or shadow of turning.
verses.18: He willed and brought us forth by the word of truth, that we might be a kind of firstfruits of His creatures.
verses.19: Know this, brothers beloved. Let every man be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger,
verses.20: for the anger of man does not produce the righteousness of God.
verses.21: Therefore, putting aside all filthiness and all abundance of evil, receive with meekness the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.
verses.22: Be doers of the word and not merely hearers who deceive themselves.
verses.23: For if any one is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man observing the face of his natural self in a mirror,
verses.24: for he observed himself and went away and immediately forgot what he was like.
verses.25: But the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues, not being a hearer who forgets but a doer of the work, this one will be blessed in his doing.
verses.26: If any one thinks himself religious and does not bridle his tongue but deceives his heart, this man's religion is futile.
verses.27: Pure and undefiled religion before God and the Father is this: to visit orphans and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained from the world.

notes:
Notes
- v. 1: The term "διασπορᾷ" is translated as "in the dispersion," reflecting the Jewish diaspora context.
- v. 18: "ἀπαρχήν τινα" is rendered "a kind of firstfruits," acknowledging the metaphor's agricultural roots.
- v. 26: "θρησκὸς" is translated as "religious" in the sense of one who is devoted to worship or ritual; the distinction between external and internal devotion is preserved.
